A failed `minds launch-to-first-message` run is no longer announced in Slack as a benign skip.

`notify_slack` classified the run by scanning `build`, `launch_to_msg`, `macos_launch` and `update_marker`. A job that gates the rest leaves its dependents `skipped` rather than `failure`, so when a gating job failed nothing in that list looked broken, `should_run` came back empty, and the message fell through to `:fast_forward: skipped` with both SHA fields blank and two commit links pointing at `/commit/`. That is exactly what happened to the 0.3.10 release's tag run: `sync_vendor` failed, and the run was reported to the channel as skipped in 23s. `sync_vendor` was not even among the jobs `notify_slack` depended on, so its result was invisible.

Every job is now scanned, including the gating ones, so a failure anywhere reports as a failure and names the job. The run is identified even when it dies before `check_should_run` publishes anything, by falling back to the ref and SHA `sync_vendor` resolved; a SHA that never resolved renders as `unresolved` instead of empty backticks, and its commit link is omitted rather than emitted broken.

The emoji now answers whether the pair is good rather than whether jobs ran, so a skip carries the success mark and only the verdict word says nothing needed rerunning. A skip means the marker cache already holds that pair, which is a healthy outcome; giving it a glyph of its own made it read as a third state next to success and failure and forced the reader into the words to find out whether anything was wrong. Successful runs are unchanged, byte for byte.
